actors.bio: A 58-year-old retired SBS bus driver. No prior cardiac history. Collapses outside a coffee shop on his morning kopi run.
The patient's wife. Works part-time at a community club. Arrives at SGH ~40 minutes after the ambulance, accompanied by her son. Lead family decision-maker for the consent conversations.
The patient's adult son, a logistics manager. Drives his mother to SGH and acts as the family liaison through the ward stay and discharge planning.
A passer-by trained in DARE (Dispatcher-Assisted first REsponder). Calls 995 and starts hands-only CPR while waiting for the AED.
Community First Responder dispatched via the SCDF myResponder app. Carries a PAD AED and arrives ahead of the ambulance.
Coffee shop attendant who clears tables and keeps onlookers back so the CFR can work. Singapore CPR culture in action.
SCDF Advanced Care Paramedic. Runs the 12-lead ECG, transmits the STEMI alert, manages airway and IV en route.
Emergency Ambulance driver. Routes via the optimal corridor and pre-notifies the receiving hospital for blue-call triage.
Receives the prehospital handover, confirms the STEMI on the repeat ECG, activates the cath team via the 24/7 STEMI pager line.
Establishes a second IV, draws bloods (troponin, FBC, U&E, APTT) in parallel with transfer to the cath lab.
Healthcare Assistant. Performs the repeat 12-lead ECG, takes vital signs, supports the nursing team during fast-track triage.
Registration clerk. Confirms identity via NRIC, opens the inpatient record, calls the next-of-kin from the patient's phone contacts.
NHCS interventional cardiologist on STEMI call. Performs the diagnostic angiogram, leads the heart-team discussion, executes the PCI.
Scrubs in, monitors haemodynamics, hands instruments, records the procedure log.
Operates the C-arm, optimises views for the operator, manages radiation dose.
Cardiac CT and MRI radiographer. Operates the scanner, manages gating, supervises contrast and gadolinium injections.
Nurse covering the imaging suite. Administers IV contrast / gadolinium, monitors the patient during scans.
Senior cardiologist leading the heart-team discussion. Chairs the family conference, explains options in plain Mandarin.
On-call cardiothoracic surgeon. Reviews angiogram for surgical candidacy. Declines CABG when anatomy and SYNTAX score favour PCI.
Consultant cardiologist leading the daily ward round. Reviews the case, sets the management plan, communicates with the family.
Registrar on the cardiology team. Pre-rounds before the consultant, writes daily plans, manages overnight issues.
Junior doctor on the ward. Clerks new admissions, takes daily bloods, writes discharge summaries.
Ward staff nurse. Responsible for medication administration, monitoring, and patient education.
Healthcare Assistant. Vital signs, bathing, mobilisation support, feeding assistance.
Phase I cardiac rehab on the ward. Early mobilisation, breathing exercises, activity progression.
Assesses activities of daily living, plans for the home environment, advises on energy conservation.
Reviews dietary history, plans the cardiac-protective diet, counsels on sodium, lipids, weight.
Reviews medication regimens for interactions, renal dose adjustments, pre-discharge counselling.
Discharge planner. Coordinates cardiac rehab referral, home setup, financial counselling, outpatient appointments.
Dispenses discharge medications, counsels the patient on dosing, side effects, and adherence.
NHCS Phase II cardiac rehab. Supervises monitored exercise sessions, prescribes home programmes.
Outpatient cardiology specialist. Reviews ECG / echo, medication compliance; titrates therapy; plans follow-up imaging.
Terminal-cleans the cath lab between cases. Turnover time directly drives how soon the next STEMI patient gets a slot — every minute counts in a 24/7 PCI service.
Cleans wards, isolation rooms, and bed-spaces between admissions. Two-step disinfection, colour-coded cloths, daily morning round.
Prepares cardiac-protective trays (low-salt, low-fat) as ordered by the dietitian. Halal and vegetarian options stocked by default.
Manages the linen par level for the wards. Stockouts delay bed turnover and stall new admissions; par level is rechecked each shift handover.
Itemises the bill, computes MediShield Life claim eligibility, the subsidy band for the ward class, the MediSave drawdown cap; explains the cash component to the family.

beats.action: Walking to the kopi counter — clutches chest, collapses.
Sees the collapse, shouts for help, dials 995.
Clears tables and keeps onlookers back so the area is safe.
On 995: dispatcher confirms cardiac arrest. Starts hands-only CPR.
Pulseless. Receiving chest compressions at 100–120 / min.
myResponder ping accepted — arrives with PAD AED from 280 m away.
AED pads on. Shock advised. Stand clear, shock delivered.
CPR resumed. Second cycle.
Return of spontaneous circulation. Groaning. Pulse palpable.

branchPoint.prompt: The 12-lead shows anterior STEMI. Where does this patient go?

options.label: SGH — primary PCI centre, cath team activated
options.hint: STEMI network destination. Bypasses the regular ED; bloods + cath in parallel.

options.label: Nearest A&E (private) — no on-site cath
options.hint: Faster door, but the patient needs a secondary transfer that delays reperfusion.

beats.action: On the stretcher — pale, post-arrest, responding to voice.
Arrives with EA. Hands over from CFR — ROSC, GCS 14.
Sets up the stretcher and clears the route to the EA.
12-lead ECG: ST elevation V1–V4. Calls STEMI alert.
IV access established. Aspirin 300 mg PO loaded.
Patient loaded. Code 3 transport. Pre-notifies receiving hospital.
En route: O2 maintained, BP 102 / 64, HR 88. ECG re-checked.
Cath team activation confirmed. ETA 4 minutes.
On the resus trolley — anterior STEMI, post-arrest, GCS 14.
Pulls into the SGH bypass bay. "STEMI bypass" called overhead.
Verbal handover: ROSC 08:21, GCS 14, BP 102/64, ECG anterior STEMI.
Patient transferred onto trolley. Repeat 12-lead leads attached.
Confirms anterior STEMI on the repeat ECG. Pages STEMI 7777.
Second IV, draws troponin + FBC + U&E + APTT in parallel.
Receives page in the cath lab; ETA to lab 4 minutes.
Registers patient via NRIC; calls Mrs Tan from the patient's mobile.
On the cath table — awake, draped, right wrist prepped.
Meets patient at the lab; brief introduction in dialect.
Gowns patient, attaches monitoring; right radial access prep.
Mrs Tan on the phone — verbal consent for emergency angiography captured.
Positions the C-arm; final dose-area-product check.
Patient on table. Ready to start. Door-to-balloon clock: 27 min.
On the cath table through the diagnostic study — haemodynamically stable.
Radial puncture; JR4 catheter; selective RCA injection.
Fluoro: mid-RCA 70% stenosis, not acute.
JL4 to left system: LAD 95% proximal — the culprit lesion.
LCx 50% non-culprit. Multivessel pattern.
Records procedure log; haemodynamics stable on heparin.
Diagnostic angiogram complete. Pause for heart-team workup.

branchPoint.prompt: CTA shows triple-vessel disease with high calcium score. Include cardiac MRI for myocardial viability before the family conference?

options.label: Yes — add cardiac MRI now
options.hint: Viability assessment confirms whether revascularising the LAD territory will recover function. Adds ~30 min.

options.label: No — proceed straight to family conference
options.hint: Faster to the decision conversation, but the team will be reasoning without LGE viability data.

beats.action: On the CT table, sliding into the gantry for the scan.
Patient slides into the CT scanner. Rate control with metoprolol IV.
IV contrast 60 mL Iopromide. Breath-hold instructions in Mandarin.
CTA acquired: triple-vessel disease, Agatston calcium score 480.
Reviews CTA with the heart team on the imaging viewer.
Pauses: cardiac MRI for viability? Decision for the team.
On the MRI table — cardiac coils placed, sliding into the bore.
Patient on the MRI table. Cardiac coils placed.
Gadolinium IV for late gadolinium enhancement.
Cine, T2, late-gad sequences acquired.
Reviews MRI: viable myocardium in LAD territory, minimal scar.
Viability confirmed. PCI is meaningful. Heart team to convene.

branchPoint.prompt: The heart team reviews findings. Multivessel disease, viable LAD territory. What does the team recommend?

options.label: Proceed to PCI now (DES to LAD)
options.hint: Single-lesion culprit, viable myocardium, time-sensitive. Non-culprit RCA managed medically.

options.label: Refer for CABG (multivessel)
options.hint: Diabetic + multivessel pattern can favour surgery. The CT surgeon will assess candidacy.

beats.action: Arrives, anxious. Family-son interprets quietly.
Sits beside his mother, translating quietly.
Explains anterior STEMI in plain Mandarin. Opens the angiogram on screen.
Shows the LAD lesion; describes the heart-team options.
Reviews the angiogram on screen; weighs surgical risk against PCI.
Describes PCI: angioplasty + drug-eluting stent, RCA managed medically.
Asks about risk; consultant-cardio answers. Ready to decide.
Reviews SYNTAX score, EuroSCORE II, patient age 58.
Declines CABG: anatomy favours PCI; surgical risk is no better.
Accepts the patient back for primary PCI.
Re-counsels family; single-lesion PCI proceeding now.
Back on the cath table for the intervention — awake, monitored.
Back on table. Wire across the LAD lesion.
Pre-dilatation balloon. Lesion opens; TIMI 2 flow restored.
Drug-eluting stent loaded: 3.5 × 24 mm.
Stent deployed; post-dilatation. Final injection — TIMI 3 flow.
Total fluoro time 12 min; dose 1.2 Gy.
Sheath haemostasis. Patient to CCU. Door-to-balloon: 89 min.
Enters with turnover trolley; next case slot already booked.
Settled into the CCU bed post-PCI — drowsy, comfortable, monitored.
Receives patient. Attaches CCU monitoring; arterial line maintained.
Clerks admission. Insulin sliding scale (newly diagnosed diabetic).
Medication reconciliation: ASA, ticagrelor, atorvastatin, bisoprolol, ramipril.
Visits bedside. Holds her husband's hand. Brief and quiet.
Mid-shift wipe-down of room edges. Discreet, efficient.
Day 2 — sitting up in bed, chest pain settled, troponin trending down.
07:00 — vital signs round before the doctors arrive.
Pre-rounds: troponin trending down, ECG resolved, no chest pain overnight.
08:30 — leads the cardiology team round. Plan: mobilise, titrate ramipril.
Phase I rehab: mobilise to bedside chair, breathing exercises.
Home assessment; advises energy conservation for stairs at home.
Cardiac-protective diet briefing: sodium < 5 g/day, lipid education.
Delivers the dietitian-ordered tray (low-salt, low-fat).
New chest tightness at rest; calls for the nurse.
GTN sublingual given; repeat ECG ordered urgently.
ECG: dynamic T-wave inversion in I + aVL. Stat troponin sent.
Calls cath-cardio overnight; non-occlusive event, manage medically.
Optimises ticagrelor dose; adds long-acting nitrate.
Next morning: pattern settled. Discharge planning in 24 h if stable.
Day 4 — up and dressed at the bedside, ready to go home.
Discharge round. Medication plan, follow-up, red flags walked through.
Books NHCS Phase II cardiac rehab; arranges outpatient cardiology in 8 weeks.
Counsels on each new med; ticagrelor dyspnoea caution; bleeding precautions.
Itemised bill: MediShield Life claim filed; MediSave drawdown; subsidy applied.
Bed turnover starts as Mr Tan dresses to leave.
At the pharmacy counter with his wife to collect the discharge meds.
Verifies prescription against discharge summary.
Dispenses 4-week supply. Walks through dose, timing, side effects.
Pays the cash portion; receipts and refill plan handed over.
Confirms next refill at the 4-week mark.
On the treadmill for the first supervised, monitored session.
Greets Mr Tan for the first supervised session.
6-minute walk test: 360 m, ~4.2 METs.
Prescribes monitored treadmill at 70% HR reserve.
Borg perceived-exertion check; BP unchanged.
Education: smoking cessation, diet review, Healthier-SG support group.
Schedules an 8-week monitored programme.
Seated on the exam couch for his 8-week specialist review.
Reviews symptoms, exercise tolerance, medication adherence.
Repeat 12-lead and echo: LVEF improved from 35% to 50%.
Continues DAPT to 12 months; statin titrated.
Non-culprit RCA: medical management; target LDL < 1.4 mmol/L.
Books 6-month review; encourages rehab maintenance.

chapters.title: Back of house — a day in the life
chapters.location: SGH back-of-house — kitchens, laundry, billing, cath turnover

beats.action: 06:00 — cath lab daily prep. Up to 24 turnovers per day depends on tight disinfection.
06:30 — first meal cycle for Ward 73. Cardiac + halal + vegetarian + diabetic variants pre-prepped.
07:00 — Ward 73 linen par recheck; replenished ahead of daily admissions.
08:00 — vitals round before the consultant round. Patients ready for the team.
09:00 — daily ward clean. High-touch surfaces with chlorine wipes.
12:00 — lunch service. Trays out via the tea trolley.
14:00 — mid-day batch. Insurance claims filed for the day's discharges.
16:00 — dirty-linen pickup. Clean linen restocked for the night shift.
On the A&E trolley — anterior STEMI confirmed, awaiting transfer.
Alternative routing: nearest A&E. ECG handed to A&E doctor.
A&E assesses; confirms anterior STEMI; no on-site cath service.
Secondary transfer to SGH cath lab activated; second alert sent.
Patient reloaded into the ambulance. Lights and siren for the transfer.
On the stretcher for the secondary transfer to SGH.
Re-runs ECG en route; no change.
Pre-notifies SGH bypass bay; ETA 8 minutes.
Door-to-balloon clock now over the 90-minute target due to the detour.
Handover prepared; SGH cath team confirms readiness.
